queries.title: Q3. SAME-DAY CHECK
queries.sql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Q3. SAME-DAY CHECK
-- Question: How many "second orders" fall on the same calendar day as the
--           first? What is the repeat rate if only a return on a later
--           day counts?
-- Logic:    same-day share = second orders with days_to_second = 0 / all
--           second orders. Later-day repeat = customers with ANY delivered
--           order on a later calendar day (first_later_day_return_at is not
--           NULL). A customer whose 2nd order was same-day but whose 3rd was
--           later still counts.
-- Result:   827 of 2,789 second orders (29.65%) are same-day.
--           Repeat rate, any day:   2,789 / 93,104 = 3.00%
--           Repeat rate, later day: 2,005 / 93,104 = 2.15%
-- =============================================================================
CREATE TEMP VIEW q3_same_day_check AS
SELECT
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM second_orders)                                   AS second_orders,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM second_orders WHERE days_to_second = 0)          AS same_day_second_orders,
    (SELECT ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE days_to_second = 0) / COUNT(*), 2)
       FROM second_orders)                                                 AS same_day_pct_of_second_orders,
    COUNT(*)                                                               AS customers,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_orders >= 2)                          AS repeat_customers_any_day,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_orders >= 2) / COUNT(*), 2)
                                                                           AS repeat_rate_any_day_pct,
    COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE first_later_day_return_at IS NOT NULL)          AS repeat_customers_later_day,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE first_later_day_return_at IS NOT NULL) / COUNT(*), 2)
                                                                           AS repeat_rate_later_day_pct
FROM delivered_customers;

\copy (SELECT * FROM q3_same_day_check) TO 'results/10_same_day_check.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
SELECT * FROM q3_same_day_check;

annotations.line: FROM delivered_customers;
annotations.note: One row per customer: delivered_customers collapses each customer's delivered orders, with the date of the first return on a LATER day (MIN(purchased_at) FILTER (WHERE purchase_date > first_purchase_date)).

annotations.line: (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM second_orders WHERE days_to_second = 0)          AS same_day_second_orders,
annotations.note: Second orders on the same calendar day as the first; days_to_second comes from LAG over the customer's delivered orders.

annotations.line: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE delivered_orders >= 2)                          AS repeat_customers_any_day,
annotations.note: Any-day repeat: two or more delivered orders, even if placed minutes apart.

annotations.line: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE first_later_day_return_at IS NOT NULL)          AS repeat_customers_later_day,
annotations.note: Later-day repeat (decision C12): at least one delivered order on a later calendar day.

queries.title: Q6. SELLER HANDLING
queries.sql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Q6. SELLER HANDLING
-- Question: How often does the seller hand the order to the carrier after
--           the shipping limit, and are those orders late more often?
-- Logic:    latest_shipping_limit = the latest shipping_limit_date among the
--           order's items (v_order_items_agg). Handover is "after the limit"
--           when order_delivered_carrier_date > latest_shipping_limit
--           (timestamp comparison). Orders with no carrier date are left
--           out and counted. Compare the late-delivery rate for the two
--           groups. This shows an association only.
-- Result:   After limit: 8,581 orders (8.92%), late rate 21.10%, median
--           16.88 days. On or before: 87,621 (91.08%), late rate 5.39%,
--           median 9.82 days. No carrier date: 1 order.
-- =============================================================================
CREATE TEMP VIEW q6_seller_handling AS
WITH h AS (
    SELECT
        is_late,
        delivery_days,
        CASE
            WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date IS NULL
              OR latest_shipping_limit IS NULL                      THEN 'no carrier date'
            WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date > latest_shipping_limit THEN 'after limit'
            ELSE 'on or before limit'
        END AS handover
    FROM timed_orders
)
SELECT
    handover,
    COUNT(*)                                                                          AS orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2)                                AS pct_of_orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_late) / COUNT(*), 2)                      AS late_rate_pct,
    ROUND((percentile_cont(0.5) WITHIN GROUP (ORDER BY delivery_days))::numeric, 2)   AS median_delivery_days
FROM h
GROUP BY handover;

\copy (SELECT * FROM q6_seller_handling ORDER BY handover) TO 'results/11_seller_handling.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
SELECT * FROM q6_seller_handling ORDER BY handover;

annotations.line: OR latest_shipping_limit IS NULL                      THEN 'no carrier date'
annotations.note: Orders without a carrier date can't be judged, so they get their own group instead of being silently dropped.

annotations.line: WHEN order_delivered_carrier_date > latest_shipping_limit THEN 'after limit'
annotations.note: Late handover: the carrier received the order after the seller's latest shipping deadline.

annotations.line: ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (), 2)                                AS pct_of_orders,
annotations.note: Share of orders: the group count divided by the grand total, a window SUM over the grouped counts.

annotations.line: ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE is_late) / COUNT(*), 2)                      AS late_rate_pct,
annotations.note: Late-delivery rate inside each handover group (calendar-day rule).

queries.title: Q8. REVIEW TIMING
queries.sql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Q8. REVIEW TIMING
-- Question: How often is the review created before the order was delivered,
--           and how do those reviews score?
-- Logic:    Delivered orders with a delivery date only. Compare calendar
--           days, because review_creation_date is almost always 00:00:00:
--           "before delivery" = review date < delivered date. Groups:
--           on-time / late x before / on-or-after delivery. pct_within is
--           the share inside the on-time or late group.
-- Result:   On time: 221 (0.25%) reviewed before delivery, low 17.65%;
--           88,961 (99.75%) on or after, low 9.23%.
--           Late: 4,749 (74.46%) reviewed BEFORE delivery, avg 1.84, low
--           75.22%; 1,629 (25.54%) on or after, avg 3.53, low 25.11%.
-- =============================================================================
CREATE TEMP VIEW q8_review_timing AS
SELECT
    CASE WHEN is_late THEN 'late' ELSE 'on_time' END                            AS delivery_group,
    CASE WHEN review_creation_date::date < order_delivered_customer_date::date
         THEN 'before delivery' ELSE 'on or after delivery' END                 AS review_timing,
    COUNT(*)                                                                    AS orders,
    ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY is_late), 2)      AS pct_within_delivery_group,
    ROUND(AVG(review_score), 2)                                                 AS avg_score,
    ROUND(100.0 * AVG(is_low_review), 2)                                        AS low_review_pct
FROM reviewed_orders
WHERE has_delivery_timing
GROUP BY is_late, 2;

\copy (SELECT * FROM q8_review_timing ORDER BY delivery_group DESC, review_timing) TO 'results/12_review_timing.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
SELECT * FROM q8_review_timing ORDER BY delivery_group DESC, review_timing;

annotations.line: CASE WHEN review_creation_date::date < order_delivered_customer_date::date
annotations.note: Review created on a calendar day before the parcel arrived.

annotations.line: ROUND(100.0 * COUNT(*) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER (PARTITION BY is_late), 2)      AS pct_within_delivery_group,
annotations.note: PARTITION BY is_late makes the share add up to 100% within on-time and within late orders separately.

annotations.line: ROUND(100.0 * AVG(is_low_review), 2)                                        AS low_review_pct
annotations.note: is_low_review is 1 for a 1-2 star review and 0 otherwise, so its average is the low-review share.

annotations.line: WHERE has_delivery_timing
annotations.note: Only delivered orders with a delivery date can be compared with the review date.

queries.title: Q1. CONCENTRATION
queries.sql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Q1. CONCENTRATION
-- Question: How much revenue comes from the biggest sellers?
-- Logic:    Rank sellers by revenue (highest first; seller_id breaks ties).
--           Running SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY rank) / total revenue =
--           cumulative share. "Top p%" = the first CEIL(p * sellers)
--           sellers, and its share is the cumulative share at that rank.
--           The full ranking is saved for a Lorenz-style chart.
-- Result:   2,945 sellers (matches baseline active sellers).
--           Top 1% (30 sellers)   = 25.93% of revenue
--           Top 5% (148)          = 52.99%
--           Top 10% (295)         = 67.04%
--           Top 20% (589)         = 82.20%
-- =============================================================================
CREATE TEMP VIEW seller_revenue_rank AS
SELECT
    seller_id,
    revenue,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, seller_id)                        AS revenue_rank,
    COUNT(*)     OVER ()                                                        AS total_sellers,
    -- Running total: sum of revenue from rank 1 down to this row
    SUM(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, seller_id
                       ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)       AS cumulative_revenue,
    SUM(revenue) OVER ()                                                        AS total_revenue
FROM seller_stats;

\copy (SELECT revenue_rank, seller_id, revenue, ROUND(100.0 * cumulative_revenue / total_revenue, 4) AS cumulative_share_pct FROM seller_revenue_rank ORDER BY revenue_rank) TO 'results/13_seller_revenue_rank.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)

CREATE TEMP VIEW q1_concentration AS
SELECT
    p.top_pct,
    r.revenue_rank                                             AS sellers_in_group,
    r.total_sellers,
    ROUND(100.0 * r.cumulative_revenue / r.total_revenue, 2)   AS revenue_share_pct
FROM (VALUES (1), (5), (10), (20)) AS p(top_pct)             -- the four cut-offs
JOIN seller_revenue_rank r
  ON r.revenue_rank = CEIL(r.total_sellers * p.top_pct / 100.0);

\copy (SELECT * FROM q1_concentration ORDER BY top_pct) TO 'results/13_concentration.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
SELECT * FROM q1_concentration ORDER BY top_pct;

annotations.line: ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY revenue DESC, seller_id)                        AS revenue_rank,
annotations.note: Rank sellers by revenue, biggest first; seller_id breaks ties so the ranking is always the same.

annotations.line: ROWS BETWEEN UNBOUNDED PRECEDING AND CURRENT ROW)       AS cumulative_revenue,
annotations.note: Running total: revenue of every seller from rank 1 down to this one.

annotations.line: FROM (VALUES (1), (5), (10), (20)) AS p(top_pct)             -- the four cut-offs
annotations.note: A four-row inline table of the cut-offs to report.

annotations.line: ON r.revenue_rank = CEIL(r.total_sellers * p.top_pct / 100.0);
annotations.note: Read the cumulative share at the last seller inside each top p%.

queries.title: Q1. MONTHLY TREND AND YEAR-ON-YEAR
queries.sql:
-- =============================================================================
-- Q1. MONTHLY TREND AND YEAR-ON-YEAR
-- Question: How did orders, revenue and AOV move month by month, and how
--           does Jan-Aug 2018 compare with Jan-Aug 2017?
-- Logic:    Q1a: group by purchase month. LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY month)
--           returns the previous month's revenue on each row; MoM change =
--           (this - previous) / previous. The first month has no previous,
--           so its change is NULL.
--           Q1b: sum each 8-month period, then compare.
-- Result:   Q1a: revenue climbs through 2017 to a peak of 987,765.37 in
--           2017-11 (+52.37% MoM), then drops -26.50% in 2017-12. In 2018
--           monthly revenue stays between 826,437.13 and 977,544.69; MoM
--           changes are -12.43% to +27.36%. AOV ranges 124.38-149.06.
--           Q1b: Jan-Aug 2018 vs 2017: orders 21,998 -> 52,783 (+139.94%),
--           revenue 2,993,456.13 -> 7,218,125.12 (+141.13%), AOV 136.08 ->
--           136.75 (+0.49%). Growth came from more orders, not bigger ones.
-- =============================================================================
CREATE TEMP VIEW q1a_monthly AS
WITH m AS (
    SELECT
        purchase_month,
        COUNT(*)          AS orders,
        SUM(item_value)   AS revenue
    FROM delivered
    GROUP BY purchase_month
)
SELECT
    purchase_month,
    orders,
    revenue,
    ROUND(revenue / orders, 2)                                         AS aov,
    LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY purchase_month)                        AS prev_month_revenue,
    ROUND(100.0 * (revenue - LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY purchase_month))
          / LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY purchase_month), 2)            AS revenue_mom_pct
FROM m;

\copy (SELECT * FROM q1a_monthly ORDER BY purchase_month) TO 'results/14_monthly_revenue.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
SELECT * FROM q1a_monthly ORDER BY purchase_month;

CREATE TEMP VIEW q1b_yoy AS
WITH p AS (
    SELECT
        COUNT(*)        FILTER (WHERE purchase_month BETWEEN DATE '2017-01-01' AND DATE '2017-08-01') AS orders_2017,
        COUNT(*)        FILTER (WHERE purchase_month BETWEEN DATE '2018-01-01' AND DATE '2018-08-01') AS orders_2018,
        SUM(item_value) FILTER (WHERE purchase_month BETWEEN DATE '2017-01-01' AND DATE '2017-08-01') AS revenue_2017,
        SUM(item_value) FILTER (WHERE purchase_month BETWEEN DATE '2018-01-01' AND DATE '2018-08-01') AS revenue_2018
    FROM delivered
)
SELECT
    orders_2017,
    orders_2018,
    ROUND(100.0 * (orders_2018 - orders_2017) / orders_2017, 2)                         AS orders_change_pct,
    revenue_2017,
    revenue_2018,
    ROUND(100.0 * (revenue_2018 - revenue_2017) / revenue_2017, 2)                      AS revenue_change_pct,
    ROUND(revenue_2017 / orders_2017, 2)                                                AS aov_2017,
    ROUND(revenue_2018 / orders_2018, 2)                                                AS aov_2018,
    ROUND(100.0 * ((revenue_2018 / orders_2018) - (revenue_2017 / orders_2017))
          / (revenue_2017 / orders_2017), 2)                                            AS aov_change_pct
FROM p;

\copy (SELECT * FROM q1b_yoy) TO 'results/14_yoy_jan_aug.csv' WITH (FORMAT csv, HEADER true)
SELECT * FROM q1b_yoy;

annotations.line: LAG(revenue) OVER (ORDER BY purchase_month)                        AS prev_month_revenue,
annotations.note: LAG puts the previous month's revenue on each row for the month-over-month change.

annotations.line: COUNT(*)        FILTER (WHERE purchase_month BETWEEN DATE '2017-01-01' AND DATE '2017-08-01') AS orders_2017,
annotations.note: FILTER counts only Jan-Aug 2017 orders in the same pass that counts 2018.

annotations.line: ROUND(100.0 * (revenue_2018 - revenue_2017) / revenue_2017, 2)                      AS revenue_change_pct,
annotations.note: Year-on-year revenue change over the same eight months.

annotations.line: / (revenue_2017 / orders_2017), 2)                                            AS aov_change_pct
annotations.note: Average order value change: shows whether growth came from bigger orders or more orders.
